title: Resolving Nonlocal State Reduction via Induced Coherence in Frequency-Comb Biphoton Sources
abstract: How macroscopic definite outcomes and nonlocal correlations emerge from entangled superpositions across spacelike-separated regions without superluminal action or {\it ad hoc} wavefunction collapse remains a defining open question in the foundations of quantum mechanics. Here, we resolve this century-long paradox within \textit{linear} relativistic quantum electrodynamics by developing an open-system and measurement-defined framework realized in dual, spacelike-separated nonlinear crystals driven synchronously by a multi-mode optical frequency comb and seeded by an ultra-narrow coherent laser. Expanding the transverse electromagnetic vector potential into discrete single-photon frequency-comb supermodes, we show that tracing out the unmeasured continuous-wave idler field yields an exact spatial dephasing Lindblad master equation whose decoherence rate is governed by the non-orthogonal state overlap of single-photon-added coherent states. Connecting this open-system map to free-vector-space quotient measurement theory, we demonstrate that single-particle interference arises from the geometric projection of the composite state onto detector-defined conditional cosets rather than remote collapse, establishing strict operational equivalence across pump, seed, and signal phase scans. The resulting wave-particle-entanglement triality equality $P^2 + E^2 + V^2 = 1$ is saturated across the complete parameter space, while the atomic-clock-referenced comb structure anchors continuous-variable time-frequency displacement stabilizers directly at the hardware layer. Our work unifies induced coherence, Bohr's complementarity, and quotient measurement theory, providing a microscopic pathway toward fault-tolerant bosonic quantum information processing.
summary: This paper resolves a foundational paradox in quantum mechanics by showing that nonlocal correlations emerge not from instantaneous collapse, but from a geometric projection onto local subspaces defined by measurement. Using frequency-comb biphoton sources, the authors model this process via an open-system Lindblad equation, unifying concepts from complementarity and quotient measurement theory.
main_problem: The paper addresses the foundational paradox of how macroscopic definite outcomes and nonlocal correlations emerge from entangled superpositions without invoking superluminal action or ad hoc wavefunction collapse.
main_result: It resolves this by demonstrating that single-particle interference arises from a geometric projection onto detector-defined conditional cosets, establishing operational equivalence with local subspace filtering rather than remote collapse.
method: The authors develop an open-system framework using Lindblad master equations and connect it to free-vector-space quotient measurement theory to model state reduction.
model_or_system: The physical platform is a dual, spacelike-separated nonlinear crystal driven by a multi-mode optical frequency comb, realizing a continuous-variable time-frequency Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (TF-GKP) logical qubit.
key_observables: The wave-particle-entanglement triality equality ($P^2 + E^2 + V^2 = 1$), interference visibility ($V$), and the invariant phase $\Delta\Phi$.
important_parameters: The decoherence rate $\Gamma_{	ext{deph}}$, the seed photon number $|\alpha|^2$, and the balance ratio $\gamma$.
main_assumptions: The framework assumes that the physical system dynamics can be accurately modeled by an open-system map derived from tracing out unmeasured continuous-wave idler fields.
figures_summary: Figures compare standard dynamical collapse versus the Quotient View (local Coset Projection) and map the theoretical parameter space showing the saturation of the triality equality.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first defining the foundational paradox, then developing the open-system/quotient measurement framework, applying it to the physical realization in frequency-comb sources, and finally confirming the results by showing the saturation of the key mathematical identities.
why_interesting: This work provides a highly rigorous, microscopic pathway linking abstract algebraic structures (quotient spaces) to measurable quantum optics phenomena (biphoton interference), which is crucial for building fault-tolerant quantum hardware.
